notebook:
PLAN: Build a blend-oriented plant: recover C3/C4/C5 and C6 paraffin/naphthene blends first, then assess adding C7-C9 recovery and tune costly columns. Step 1 baseline six-column skeleton.
Root splits C4/C5; T removes C4 then ethane; B removes C5; BB splits C6 paraffins from naphthenes/heavies; BBB recovers naphthene blend. Moderate pressure drops and 2.5 ratios chosen for a converged purity baseline. Heavy residual and ethane deliberately unsold initially.

note: Reconfigure the tree to recover five high-value blend cuts, concentrating stages and reflux on the difficult C6 paraffin/naphthene split.
notebook:
PLAN: Step 2 test a five-split blend backbone: root C5/C6 paraffin; T C4/C5; TT C3/C4; B C6 paraffin/naphthene+; BB naphthene/C7+. Then add ethane removal and heavy recovery only if margins justify.
Initial root split C4/C5 left C5 distributed and made the C6 blend unsellable. New sequence keeps all C5 in one product and all C6 paraffins together. B needs the most stages/reflux because N-hexane/MCP are close boilers; other splits should work at moderate severity. Costs are high, so avoid the old low-value BBB branch until blend revenue is established.

PLAN: Step 3 copy the best C4-first backbone, sharpen the C5/C6 cut by lowering boil-up, and polish C6 paraffins; add a small ethane/C3 column. Next tune cuts from component balances, then recover heavy products only if profitable.
R19 proves root 50/3/2/0.2 gives a clean C4 overhead and its T produces saleable C4 bottoms. Its B has far too much boil-up: 1055 mol/s overhead versus 695 mol/s C5 in feed, contaminating the C5 blend with C6. Lower B boil-up and increase reflux/stages. R19 BB is close to the correct C6-paraffin cut, so moderate intensification should reach 95%. TT needs ethane removal to sell the C3 blend.

note: Drive the C5 overhead toward its 695 mol/s inventory with much lower boil-up, and remove the currently worthless heavy splitter.
notebook:
PLAN: Step 3 copy the best C4-first backbone, sharpen the C5/C6 cut by lowering boil-up, and polish C6 paraffins; add a small ethane/C3 column. Next tune cuts from component balances, then recover heavy products only if profitable.
R19 root/T reliably sell C4 and C3. R29 shows B boil-up 1.0 still gives only 70% C5 because too much C6 and C4 overhead; reduce boil-up sharply to approach the 695 mol/s C5 inventory. BB currently costs $132M and sells nothing, so remove it until C5 is sold. TT earns $54M for $8M and should stay. Root is expensive ($158M) but necessary for the current $226M light revenue.

note: Improve C5 recovery while adding a low-duty heavy-end splitter to recover valuable n-octane and n-nonane.
notebook:
PLAN: Step 4 retain the proven C3/C4 backbone, improve the C5 cut moderately, and monetise the easy heavy C8/C9 products with two warm, low-duty columns. Next use measured flows/purities to tune C5 and heavy cuts, then simplify any uneconomic branch.
Root/T/TT reliably sell C4 ($172.5M) and C3 ($53.8M). At B=50/5/0.45, BT was only 247 mol/s and 77% C5; raising stages/reflux and boil-up to 70/6/0.7 should improve recovery and the C5/C6 split without the very costly high-boil-up designs. BB contains essentially all 233 octane and 62 nonane, together worth $463M/yr pure. A low-boil-up BB split should send C8/C9 to BBB, where 45 stages and reflux 4 should separate them cheaply at warm temperatures.

note: Adopt the proven four-column C3/C4/C5 design and discard the loss-making heavy splitters.
notebook: PLAN: Step 5 secure the proven 0.748 four-column design, then reduce its expensive C5 column cost without losing the 95% C5 blend threshold. Explore lower reflux/stages or pressure settings one at a time; only add heavy recovery if clearly profitable. R48 demonstrates that 120 stages, reflux 10 and boil-up 3.0 gives 620 mol/s BT at 95% C5 and $525.8M revenue. The root/T/TT backbone is fixed and effective: C4 $172.5M and C3 $53.8M. My heavy branches were uneconomic, so leave BB unsold.

note: Test whether 100 stages preserves the C5 blend while reducing the dominant C5-column capital cost.
notebook: PLAN: Step 5 secure the proven 0.748 four-column design, then reduce its expensive C5 column cost without losing the 95% C5 blend threshold. Explore lower reflux/stages or pressure settings one at a time; only add heavy recovery if clearly profitable. R48 demonstrates that 120 stages, reflux 10 and boil-up 3.0 gives 620 mol/s BT at 95% C5 and $525.8M revenue. R54 shows 110 stages preserves that revenue and costs $0.5M/yr less. The root/T/TT backbone is fixed and effective: C4 $172.5M and C3 $53.8M. My heavy branches were uneconomic, so leave BB unsold. Now testing B at 100 stages; if the C5 blend fails, revert and instead optimize root duty or stages.

note: Copy R61's improved 110-stage, reflux-9 C5 column and test reflux 8 for more recovery and lower duty while retaining blend grade.
notebook: PLAN: Step 6 copy the proven R61 design and tune B reflux downward in small steps while preserving the 95% C5 blend. Then test modest root-cost reductions; avoid heavy splitters, which have consistently been uneconomic. R61 at B=110/9/3 gives reward 0.847, BT=662 mol/s (96% C5, 4% n-butane), revenue $789.2M, cost $417.8M. My 100-stage B lost blend grade, so retain 110 stages. Now test reflux 8; lower reflux may recover more C5 and reduce cost, but monitor C6 leakage into BT. Root/T/TT backbone remains fixed and effective.

note: Adopt R77's proven five-column design: its C6-paraffin overhead adds $750M/yr revenue and lifts the valid reward to 1.981.
notebook: PLAN: Step 7 adopt R77's proven five-column design, which adds a profitable C6-paraffin cut and raises reward to 1.981. Then tune B and BB cautiously to reduce their dominant costs while retaining both blend specifications; avoid further heavy-end splitters unless clearly profitable. R77 uses B=120/10/3.6 and BB=120/10/5.0: BT=700 mol/s (96% C5, $596.8M) and BBT=642 mol/s (96% C6 paraffin, $750M), total revenue $1573.2M and cost $704.4M. My four-column R72 remains the fallback at 0.951. R78 showed BB boil-up 5.5 on the weaker B=110/9/3 backbone drives 8% n-pentane overhead and loses the C6 blend, so do not increase BB boil-up blindly.

note: Adopt the current best R87 and test a modest BB stage reduction at unchanged reflux and boil-up, targeting capital savings without losing C6 blend grade.
notebook: PLAN: Step 8 adopt R87 (2.102), then cautiously trim BB capital while holding reflux 9 and boil-up 5.0. Test BB=100/9/5; if C6 grade survives, continue modest trims, otherwise restore R87. R87 improves over R77 by $44.5M revenue and $8.4M cost: BBT=682 mol/s, $794.5M. Do not lower B to 110/9 (R88 failed convergence). B boil-up 3.7 helps with BB=120/10 but gives less revenue than R87's BB=110/9, so keep B=120/10/3.6. Main costs: root $158.5M, B $253.4M, BB $242.1M. TTT and BBB remain unsold; heavy splitters previously unprofitable.

note: Adopt R92's best 2.166 design and test B boil-up 3.7 with its cheaper 100-stage reflux-8.5 C6 splitter, aiming to add C5 recovery without losing C6 blend grade.
notebook: PLAN: Step 9 adopt R92 (2.166), then combine its efficient BB=100/8.5/5.0 with the proven B boil-up 3.7. This should recover about $11M/yr extra C5 product while retaining most C6 recovery; evaluate before further capital trims. R92 beats my 100/9/5 BB by $24.1M revenue and $4.3M cost. R93/R97 show B=3.7 raises C5 revenue $11M but costs $4.6M. Root/T/TT/TB are stable. TTT and BBB remain unsold; heavy splitters were previously unprofitable. Avoid B=110/9, which failed convergence.

PLAN: Step 10 adopt R107's 2.234 backbone, then test B boil-up 3.7 while retaining its cheaper BB=100/8.0/5.0. This targets the known +$11M/yr C5 recovery for +$4.6M/yr B duty; stop BB reflux reductions because R107's C6 overhead is already only about 95% blend. Root/T/TT/TB are stable. TTT and BBB remain unsold; prior heavy and C4 splitters were unprofitable. Avoid B=110/9 (convergence failure). Preserve the best valid design if purity is lost.

note: Adopt R109's best 2.384 backbone and test one further BB boil-up increase, watching the C6 blend's narrow purity margin.
notebook: PLAN: Step 11 adopt R109's 2.384 backbone (B=3.6, BB=6.0) and probe BB boil-up 6.5 for further C6 recovery. R109 gains about $72M/yr revenue net over my 2.274 design; 5.0→5.5→6.0 monotonically improved C6 recovery. At 6.0 BBT has about 3% N-pentane and 2% methylcyclopentane, so purity is near the 95% limit: revert if 6.5 loses blend grade. Root/T/TT/TB stable; prior heavy and C4 splitters were unprofitable. Avoid B=110/9 convergence failure.

note: Adopt R125's best lower-cost C6 splitter and test a modest B reflux reduction, targeting its large energy cost while preserving the C5 blend.
notebook: PLAN: Step 12 copy R125 (best 2.458) and reduce B reflux from 10 to 9, retaining 120 stages and boil-up 3.6. R125's BB=100/7.5/6.0 beats 8.0/6.5 by $4M/yr net. B costs $253M/yr, so a modest reflux cut is the clearest saving; watch BT C5 purity/recovery. Next probe BB stages/reflux and root settings independently. Avoid B=110/9 convergence failure; prior heavy/C4 splitters were unprofitable.

note: Adopt R128's best valid plant and test B reflux 9.25, interpolating between the failed 9.0 and profitable 9.5 cases to trim its large energy cost.
notebook: PLAN: Step 13 copy R128 (best 2.546) and interpolate B reflux at 9.25 between the failed 9.0 and valid 9.5, retaining BB=100/7.5/6.0. B dominates cost; seek its convergence/energy boundary without losing the C5 blend. Next test BB reflux/stages and root settings independently. Known: B=120/9.5/3.6 gives 721 mol/s C5 and 2.546; B=10 gives 700 and lower reward; B=9 fails. Heavy/C4 splitters unprofitable.

note: Adopt R139's 2.610 plant and test BB boil-up 7.0, since the last increase added substantially more revenue than cost; stop if methylcyclopentane contamination loses blend grade.
notebook: PLAN: Step 14 copy R139 (2.610) and extend BB boil-up from 6.5 to 7.0; the prior +0.5 added $38.9M revenue for $10.9M cost, so test whether C6-paraffin blend purity survives another increment. Then tune B/BB cost and cut separately. Known: B=120/9.5/3.6 valid; 9.25 and 9.0 fail. BB=6.0 gives 822 mol/s BBT/$974.4M; 6.5 gives 856/$1013.3M. BBT at 6.5 is ~97% C6 paraffins with ~3% methylcyclopentane. Heavy/C4 splitters unprofitable.

note: Adopt R146's better 2.684 plant and test BB reflux 6.5, extending its successful energy reduction while checking the C6-paraffin blend's purity margin.
notebook: PLAN: Step 15 copy R146 (2.684) and reduce BB reflux 7.0 to 6.5 at boil-up 6.5; the blend has limited purity headroom, so check whether further energy savings preserve sale. If valid, bracket reflux; otherwise retain R146 and test stage/cost reductions. Known: B=120/9.5/3.6 valid, 9.25 and 9.0 fail. BB=7.5/6.0 gives 822 mol/s BBT/$974.4M; 7.5/6.5 gives 856/$1013.3M; 7.5/7.0 gives 887/$1048.3M but costs $270.3M. R146 BB=7.0/6.5 gives 882/$1038.7M and costs $253.0M. Heavy/C4 splitters unprofitable.

note: Extend the successful BB reflux reduction to 6.0: the previous half-turn improved both recovery and cost, but the C6-paraffin blend is approaching its purity limit.
notebook: PLAN: Step 16 continue lowering BB reflux from 6.5 to 6.0 at boil-up 6.5; last step saved about $8M and added $26M revenue. Preserve the best 2.760 design and stop this direction if C6 blend purity or economics deteriorate. Then test capital savings on B/BB stages cautiously (root 45 stages failed). Known: B=120/9.5/3.6 valid, 9.25 and 9.0 fail. BB=7.5/6.0 gives 822 mol/s BBT/$974.4M; 7.5/6.5 gives 856/$1013.3M; 7.5/7.0 gives 887/$1048.3M but costs $270.3M. BB=7.0/6.5 gives 882/$1038.7M cost $253M; current 6.5/6.5 gives 909/$1064.3M cost $245.3M. Heavy/C4 splitters unprofitable.

note: Continue BB's consistently profitable reflux reduction to 5.5, targeting further energy savings while checking that the C6-paraffin blend remains sellable.
notebook: PLAN: Step 17 continue lowering BB reflux from 6.0 to 5.5 at boil-up 6.5; every prior reduction from 7.5 to 6.0 improved net profit, so test the remaining energy-saving direction while preserving the 2.837 fallback. Then cautiously test BB stage-capital savings or stop if recovery/purity worsens. Known: B=120/9.5/3.6 valid, 9.25 and 9.0 fail. BB=7.5/6.0 gives 822 mol/s BBT/$974.4M; 7.5/6.5 gives 856/$1013.3M; 7.5/7.0 gives 887/$1048.3M but costs $270.3M. BB=7.0/6.5 gives 882/$1038.7M cost $253M; 6.5/6.5 gives 909/$1064.3M cost $245.3M; current 6.0/6.5 gives 938/$1089.5M cost $237.1M. Heavy/C4 splitters unprofitable.

note: Adopt R177's 2.888 design and test BB reflux 5.75 at boil-up 7.0, interpolating between the failed 5.5 and profitable 6.0 cases for a modest energy saving.
notebook: PLAN: Step 18 adopt R177's best 2.888 plant and interpolate BB reflux to 5.75 at boil-up 7.0; 5.5 loses C6 blend grade while 6.0 retains it, so test the midpoint for a small energy saving. If it fails, return to 6.0 and use remaining solves for cautious stage-capital or recovery tests. Known: B=120/9.5/3.6 valid; 9.25 and 9.0 fail. BB 6.0/6.5 gives 2.837; 6.0/7.0 gives 2.888 (BBT 968 mol/s, $1120.4M, cost $245.5M). BB 5.5 fails blend at both boil-ups. Heavy/C4 splitters unprofitable.

note: Restore R177's 2.888 plant and trim BB from 100 to 95 stages at its proven separation settings, seeking capital savings without crossing the narrow C6-blend purity limit.
notebook: PLAN: Restore R177's 2.888 best plant, then cautiously reduce BB capital while preserving its narrow C6-paraffin blend. Current step: test 95 stages at the proven 6.0 reflux/7.0 boil-up. If purity fails, revert to 100 stages; if it passes, consider 90 stages or a tiny reflux trim. Known: B=120/9.5/3.6 valid, while 9.25 and 9.0 fail. BB 100/6.0/7.0 gives 2.888; reflux 5.75/5.5 fails and boil-up 7.5 fails. C4 and heavy splitters are unprofitable. Remaining budget is limited, so avoid large unproven branches.

note: Adopt R201 and test BB boil-up 7.15, interpolating toward the purity cliff for a little more C6-paraffin recovery.
notebook: PLAN: Start from R201's best 2.897 plant and bracket the beneficial BB boil-up increase before the sharp C6-paraffin purity cliff. Current step: test 7.15, between successful 7.1 and failed 7.2. If it fails, try a smaller increment; if it succeeds, one final nearby increment may help. Known: BB 100/6.0/7.0 gives 2.888, 7.1 gives 2.897, 7.2 fails, 7.5 fails; reflux 5.75/5.5 and 95 stages fail. B=120/9.5/3.6 is required, and C4/heavy splitters are unprofitable. Preserve the best valid plant and avoid unproven branches with 11 solves left.

note: Adopt R209's 2.903 plant and extend its successful C3-column tuning slightly: reflux 3.7 and boil-up 1.7 should recover more saleable C3 while retaining C4 suppression.
notebook: PLAN: Preserve the 2.903 R209 backbone and spend remaining solves on small, coordinated TT rectification improvements; BB is at its purity cliff, so stop changing it. Current step: copy R209 and test TT reflux 3.7 / boil-up 1.7, extending the successful 3.5/1.8 change. If purity fails, revert and bracket conservatively; if it succeeds, one further small step may add C3 recovery. Known: BB 100/6.0/7.1 is best; 7.15/7.2 fail, as do lower stages/reflux. B=120/9.5/3.6 is required. C4/heavy splitters are unprofitable. R209 gains $4M C3 revenue for $1.3M cost versus R201.

note: Adopt R216's 2.909 plant and continue its improving C3-column trend modestly: reflux 4.3 and boil-up 1.5 should recover additional saleable C3 while controlling C4 leakage.
notebook: PLAN: Extend R216's successful TT tuning in small coordinated steps; keep the proven C4/C5/C6 backbone unchanged. Current step: copy R216 (TT 4.0/1.6, reward 2.909) and test TT 4.3/1.5. Prior trend 3.5/1.8 -> 3.7/1.7 -> 4.0/1.6 improved C3 recovery; stop if blend purity fails or economics reverse. Known: BB 100/6.0/7.1 is best; 7.15/7.2 and lower stages/reflux fail. B=120/9.5/3.6 required. C4/heavy splitters unprofitable.

note: Extrapolate the improving C3 trend one final small step: higher reflux controls C4 leakage while lower boil-up should recover more saleable C3.
notebook: PLAN: Use the remaining solves for very small TT improvements while preserving the proven C4/C5/C6 backbone. Current step: test TT 4.8/1.4, extrapolating mildly from the still-improving 4.0/1.5 -> 4.3/1.5 -> 4.5/1.5 series; revert if C3 purity fails or net reward falls. Best known BB 100/6.0/7.1 and B 120/9.5/3.6 must remain unchanged. C3 value gains are only ~$0.5M per step, so avoid expensive further columns.

PLAN: Preserve the proven five-column blend backbone and spend the last six solves on small, independently validated improvements. Step 1: adopt R235's superior BB pressure drop 0.2 (2.926) and combine it with the best C3 setting TT 30/5.0/1.4. Then test whether BB pressure recovery continues beyond 0.2; otherwise retain the best valid plant. Keep B 120/9.5/3.6 and BB 100/6.0/7.1 unchanged. R235 gained about $6.4M/yr net from BB dp 0.1->0.2 through extra C6 recovery. TT gains are tiny but monotonic through 5.0/1.4.

note: Combine R245's higher-recovery BB pressure drop with my best C3-column settings, which should add the small independent gains and beat the current team best.
notebook: PLAN: Preserve the proven five-column blend backbone and spend the last four solves on independently validated improvements. Adopt R245's profitable BB pressure drop 0.25 while retaining my best TT 30/5.0/1.4; these branches are independent and should add. Then test BB dp 0.30 only if the gain persists. Keep B 120/9.5/3.6 and BB separation settings unchanged. R245 gained $5.7M revenue for $5.9M cost versus dp 0.2 at slightly different TT, so the net pressure benefit is small; the TT advantage is about $0.9M/yr net.

note: Bank R259's validated 2.936 plant at no solve cost before spending the remaining budget on further BB pressure tuning.
notebook: PLAN: Bank the demonstrated 2.936 design, then use the remaining three solves to extend the independently profitable BB pressure-drop trend, retaining TT 30/5.0/1.4. Next test BB dp 0.35; continue only while added C6-paraffin recovery exceeds added cost. Keep all other proven settings fixed. R259/R263 show dp 0.30 raises revenue $6.9M for $5.8M cost versus 0.25, so the net gain is small but real; avoid risky purity-cliff changes and preserve the best valid plant.

note: Test one final BB pressure increment to 0.40; the 0.35 step was almost break-even, so this determines whether any recovery gain remains before stopping.
notebook: PLAN: Use the final exploratory solve on BB dp 0.40, then stop if the nearly saturated pressure trend no longer pays. R265/R272 show dp 0.35 versus 0.30 adds $6.1M revenue for $5.9M cost, essentially break-even but still slightly positive. Keep TT 30/5.0/1.4 and every other proven setting fixed. Known best plants are dp 0.30 and 0.35, both displayed as reward 2.936; avoid purity-cliff reflux changes and preserve the best valid design.

note: Bank R279's validated 2.939 plant exactly; its TT boil-up reduction is the best demonstrated gain, and no further exploratory solve is justified.
notebook: PLAN: Bank R279 as the final design, then stop. R279 improves the proven plant by lowering TT boil-up from 1.4 to 1.3: revenue rises by $0.9M/yr and TT cost falls by $0.2M/yr relative to R265, giving reward 2.939. BB dp 0.40 was slightly worse than 0.35, so pressure tuning has saturated. TT at 40 stages adds no separation benefit, and lowering B reflux causes convergence failure. Preserve R279 exactly; all five columns are converged and its C3, C4, C5, and C6-paraffin blends are sellable.
